claim_text: In one inavolisib-treated patient, phylogenetic analysis showed truncal H1047R and E726K with subclonal Q859K and AKT1 alterations at autopsy; in serial ddPCR from two patients, emergence of Q859K, W780R, and AKT1 mutations accompanied rebound of the founder H1047R mutation before or around clinical progression `pmid-37916958`.
evidence_summary: pmid-37916958 analyzed rapid-autopsy WES from an inavolisib-treated HR-positive HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer patient and serial ddPCR from two patients. It found truncal PIK3CA H1047R/E726K with subclonal PIK3CA Q859K and AKT1 alterations, and serial rebound of H1047R with emergent Q859K, W780R, and AKT1 mutations around progression. Limitation: small patient examples.

claim_text: RLY-2608, an allosteric pan-mutant-selective inhibitor, retained potency, binding, and downstream signaling inhibition in these double-mutant models because it binds outside the catalytic pocket `pmid-37916958`.
evidence_summary: pmid-37916958 engineered T47D and MCF7 cells carrying primary activating PIK3CA mutations plus W780R or Q859H/K, and assessed drug potency, binding, and downstream signaling. W780/Q859 reduced orthosteric inhibitor effects, while RLY-2608 potency, binding, and pathway inhibition were unaffected, consistent with allosteric binding outside the catalytic pocket. Limitation: no clinical rescue cohort.
reviewer_notes: Supported for the engineered double-mutant models.

claim_text: The RLY-2608 discovery paper supports the plausibility of this binding-mode distinction, but its clinical evidence consists of early proof-of-concept responses in patients with kinase- or helical-domain PIK3CA-mutant breast cancer, not a demonstrated clinical rescue cohort after secondary PIK3CA resistance `pmid-37916956`.
evidence_summary: pmid-37916956 used cryoEM, molecular dynamics, DEL screening, xenografts, insulin/C-peptide readouts, and two ReDiscover case vignettes. It shows RLY-2608 is a mutant-selective allosteric inhibitor and reports partial responses in one H1047R/E453K and one E542K HR-positive metastatic breast cancer case. Limitation: neither case is a secondary W780/Q859 post-orthosteric-resistance rescue cohort.

claim_text: In SANDPIPER ctDNA analyses of HR-positive HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer, clonal multiple PIK3CA mutations correlated with higher response and longer progression-free survival on taselisib plus fulvestrant than subclonal multiple mutations, supporting the idea that some baseline double mutations mark stronger pathway dependence rather than resistance `pmid-37101291`.
evidence_summary: pmid-37101291 analyzed baseline ctDNA from SANDPIPER HR-positive HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer patients treated with fulvestrant with or without taselisib, inferred PIK3CA mutation clonality, and assessed ORR and PFS. Clonal multiple PIK3CA mutations had fewer RTK/non-PIK3CA PI3K co-alterations and better taselisib outcomes than subclonal multiple mutations. Limitation: exploratory clonality inference and subgroup sizes.

claim_text: Mutation-spectrum studies similarly show that double PIK3CA mutations are not rare among PIK3CA-mutant breast cancers and that non-hotspot mutations such as E726K may act differently depending on whether they are isolated, paired with hotspot mutations, clonal, or subclonal `pmid-32404150`; comprehensive genomic profiling extends this point by showing that OTHERm and SOLAR1m mutations overlap clinically, that some subclonal OTHERm may represent later tumor evolution, and that clinical benefit from alpelisib can still occur outside the original hotspot set `pmid-36321996`.
evidence_summary: pmid-32404150 surveyed 6338 breast cancers and a 48-patient ctDNA cohort, finding double PIK3CA mutations in about 12% of PIK3CA-mutant breast cancers and discussing E726K as weak alone but synergistic in double mutants. pmid-36321996 used CGP and Flatiron-Foundation real-world outcomes, showing SOLAR1m/OTHERm genomic-context overlap, subclonal OTHERm possibly arising later, and rwPFS benefit with alpelisib/fulvestrant in OTHERm. Limitations: first study is mostly descriptive; second is retrospective real-world evidence.

claim_text: Because PI3K inhibitor resistance also includes PTEN loss, AKT1 activation, RTK/MAPK bypass, p110-beta compensation, and adaptive transcriptional programs, serial ctDNA or contemporary tissue profiling is essential before assigning progression to secondary PIK3CA mutation alone `pmid-31859350` `pmid-27604488`.
corrected_claim: Because PI3K inhibitor resistance can include PTEN loss, AKT activation, RTK/MAPK bypass, PI3K isoform compensation, and adaptive transcriptional programs, serial ctDNA or recent tissue profiling can help avoid overassigning progression to secondary PIK3CA mutation alone.
evidence_summary: pmid-31859350 is a biomarker review noting multiple PI3K inhibitor resistance routes and limitations of archival tissue, heterogeneous assays, and baseline-only testing; pmid-27604488 used functional screens and small paired biopsy analyses showing diverse resistance genes and multiple upregulated programs after BYL719. Limitation: neither cited source directly proves serial ctDNA or contemporary tissue profiling is essential in all cases.
reviewer_notes: The mechanistic heterogeneity is supported, but 'essential' is stronger than the cited review plus preclinical/small-biopsy evidence can establish.
